questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: Identify the organelle that produces ATP
questions.stem: Astronomer's log notes a cell with abundant mitochondria; which organelle is the main ATP producer?

options.text: Mitochondria generate ATP through cellular respiration in most eukaryotic cells

options.misconception: confuses protein synthesis with energy production

options.text: Golgi apparatus packages ATP into vesicles for export
options.misconception: confuses processing and shipping with ATP synthesis

questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the primary ATP producers in eukaryotic cells. Ribosomes make proteins, the Golgi processes and ships molecules, and lysosomes digest material.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: Explain surface-area-to-volume limits on cell size
questions.stem: Explain why a very large cell faces transport problems even with a healthy membrane.

answer.exemplar: As a cell grows, its volume increases faster than its surface area, so the membrane area available for exchange becomes too small relative to the cell's needs.

questions.explanation: Volume grows as the cube of linear size while surface area grows as the square. A huge cell cannot exchange enough nutrients and wastes across its membrane despite intact transport proteins.
questions.hint: Compare how surface area and volume scale.

answer.exemplar: The midpiece mitochondria generate ATP to power the flagellar tail's movement toward the egg.

questions.explanation: Sperm motility demands ATP, supplied by midpiece mitochondria. This links energy production to movement.

options.text: They transport sugars from leaves to roots through phloem
They provide rigid support to prevent leaf wilting

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: Interpret hypertonic solution effects
questions.stem: A log observes a cell shrinking in a solution with higher external solute concentration; what occurred?

options.text: Water left the cell by osmosis, causing shrinkage in the hypertonic solution
Water entered the cell, making it swell and then shrink
Solutes entered the cell and dissolved the membrane
options.misconception: confuses solute movement with membrane damage

options.text: No change occurred because membranes block all solutes

questions.explanation: Higher external solute concentration is hypertonic, so net water leaves the cell and it shrinks. Membranes are selectively permeable, not impermeable.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: Identify prokaryotic cell structures from a diagram
questions.stem: A log diagram shows a cell with a nucleoid region but no nucleus; which structure holds its DNA?

options.text: A membrane-bound nucleus in the center of the cell
A nucleoid region where circular DNA is concentrated
A nucleolus storing ribosomal proteins only
A cell wall layer that also stores genetic material

questions.explanation: Prokaryotic DNA is concentrated in a nucleoid region, not enclosed by a nucleus. The nucleolus and wall do not store the main genome.

questions.learningObjective: Explain nucleus role as control center
questions.stem: Explain why the nucleus is called the control center of the cell.

answer.exemplar: It stores DNA, which contains instructions for making proteins and regulating cellular activities, directing growth and reproduction.

questions.explanation: DNA in the nucleus encodes instructions that regulate protein synthesis and cellular processes, guiding cell function and division.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: Describe fluid mosaic model
questions.stem: Entry 50 references the fluid mosaic model; what does it describe?

options.text: A rigid membrane made only of cellulose fibers
A static layer of identical proteins frozen in place
A dynamic bilayer with proteins and lipids able to move laterally
A single layer of proteins without any lipid component

questions.explanation: The fluid mosaic model describes a dynamic lipid bilayer with proteins that can move laterally. It is not rigid, static, or protein-only.

questions.stem: A log table shows more chloroplasts in sun leaves than shade leaves; what does this suggest?

Chloroplasts are useless in high light and accumulate randomly
Shade leaves perform no photosynthesis at all

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: Estimate cell count from tissue volume
questions.stem: A log diagram shows a 1 mm cube of tissue made of 10 micrometer cells; roughly how many cells fit along one edge?

options.text: About 100 cells fit along one edge of the cube
About 10 cells fit because 1 mm equals 10 micrometers
About 1 cell fits because cells are macroscopic
About 1000 cells fit because 1 mm equals 1000 micrometers cubed

questions.explanation: One millimeter equals 1000 micrometers, and 1000/10 = 100 cells along one edge. Volume would be 100 cubed, not the edge count.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: Match osteocyte specialization to bone maintenance
questions.stem: Entry 53 notes cells embedded in bone matrix maintaining mineral balance; what are they?

options.text: They are osteoblasts only secreting new bone matrix
They are osteoclasts dissolving bone for calcium release
They are osteocytes maintaining bone tissue and mineral homeostasis
They are chondrocytes producing cartilage in joints
options.misconception: confuses bone cells with cartilage cells

questions.explanation: Osteocytes are mature bone cells that maintain tissue and mineral balance. Osteoblasts form bone, osteoclasts resorb it, and chondrocytes make cartilage.
questions.hint: Embedded mature bone cells are osteocytes.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: Interpret data on neuron myelination
questions.stem: A log table shows myelinated axons conducting signals faster than unmyelinated ones; what explains this?

options.text: Myelin increases axon diameter to 100 micrometers in all neurons
Myelin insulates axons and allows saltatory conduction at nodes
Myelin generates ATP to power faster signal propagation
Myelin dissolves in high salt to speed ion diffusion

questions.explanation: Myelin insulates axons, enabling saltatory conduction that jumps between nodes of Ranvier and increases speed. It does not primarily change diameter or produce ATP.

Osmosis moving water out with the hormones

options.text: Phagocytosis engulfing large particles into vesicles
Exocytosis releasing vesicle contents outside the cell

questions.explanation: Vesicle fusion with the plasma membrane releases contents outside the cell, which is exocytosis. Endocytosis and phagocytosis bring material in.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: Explain selective antibiotic targeting
questions.stem: Explain why antibiotic targets often differ between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

answer.exemplar: Antibiotics can target prokaryotic-specific structures like 70S ribosomes or cell walls without harming eukaryotic 80S ribosomes or membrane-bound cells.

questions.explanation: Structural differences allow drugs to selectively disrupt bacteria. Eukaryotic cells lack many prokaryotic targets, reducing harm to host cells.

questions.learningObjective: Identify chloroplast DNA evidence
questions.stem: Entry 59 notes chloroplasts contain their own DNA; what evolutionary inference is supported?

Chloroplasts are produced de novo by the nucleus each day
Chloroplasts likely originated from an engulfed photosynthetic prokaryote
